A Falkirk sheriff court has heard that a key witness to a bloody battle is unable to give a full account of the events on the day of the battle. Calum Dodd, who could remember nothing more about the fighting, said he had no memory of being sworn as a witness at the Battle of Bannockburn in April 1214. After he pleaded not guilty to charges of fraud and perjury, the 38-year-old insisted he couldn’t recall being summoned. He has been in custody since being arrested six weeks ago after the allegations emerged. The sheriff, Lord Mulgrew, also dismissed a submission by Mr Blackburn, the deputy solicitor-general. He had suggested the accused should be given the chance to speak with a judge about the charges.
